meta.title: The platform
meta.description: Applications, Docker Compose, databases, domains and certificates, monitoring, servers and clusters: what Notploy deploys and operates.

hero.title: Everything you deploy and operate, in a single interface
hero.lead: Notploy brings applications, their dependencies and the infrastructure that carries them together, with no install script to maintain.

applications.title: Deploy from Git or a container image
applications.lead: Each application is built and then deployed by the platform, with the build strategy you choose.

paragraphs.p1: Notploy builds your application from a Git repository or a published container image, then deploys it to the targeted server or cluster. Environment variables, volumes and resource limits are configured in the interface, in the same place as the deployment.

docker.title: Docker
docker.desc: A Dockerfile in your repository, or an already published image.

nixpacks.title: Nixpacks
nixpacks.desc: Automatic detection of the language and the build command.

railpack.title: Railpack
railpack.desc: Automatic builds of applications without a Dockerfile.

compose.title: Run your Docker Compose projects
compose.lead: One Compose file, several services: the platform drives them as a single unit.

bullets.b1: Each service exposes its configuration, its environment variables and its volumes.
bullets.b2: The logs and the state of each container stay available from the interface.
bullets.b3: Deployments and restarts are triggered without going through the server terminal.
bullets.b4: Compose projects sit next to your other applications, in the same infrastructure.

databases.title: Provision and back up your data engines
databases.lead: Notploy creates the databases your applications need and schedules their backups.

redis.title: Redis
redis.desc: In-memory store for cache and queues.

routing.title: Expose your applications on your own domains
routing.lead: Traefik is driven by the platform: routing, domains and certificates stay in the interface.

bullets.b1: Each application receives one or more domains, with their certificate.
bullets.b2: Certificates are issued and renewed automatically.
bullets.b3: Routing rules apply without restarting the rest of the infrastructure.
bullets.b4: Traffic can be exposed over HTTP, or redirected to HTTPS.

monitoring.title: Track your resources and your logs
monitoring.lead: The usage and the logs of your workloads are visible from the platform.

bullets.b1: Resource usage of the host and of the containers can be consulted continuously.
bullets.b2: The logs of each application and each service stay available in the interface.
bullets.b3: Deployment notifications go to the providers you configure.

servers.title: From the local server to the Swarm cluster
servers.lead: The platform distinguishes the machine hosting it from the machines running your workloads.

local.title: Local server
local.desc: Deploy directly to the machine running Notploy.

remote.title: Remote servers
remote.desc: Add remote machines and drive them over SSH.

swarm.title: Docker Swarm
swarm.desc: Spread your services over a Docker Swarm cluster.

meta.title: Developer space
meta.description: Automate Notploy with the REST API, the TypeScript SDK, the CLI, the MCP server, GitHub Actions and the VS Code extension.

hero.title: Automate everything the interface can do
hero.lead: Every action of the platform is exposed by an API, and comes with a SDK, a CLI, an MCP server and integrations for your tools.

api.title: The REST API of the platform
api.lead: Every operation of the platform is described by an OpenAPI specification.

paragraphs.p1: The API covers applications, deployments, databases, servers and Compose projects. The OpenAPI specification published with the project is the reference for clients and for code generation.

bullets.b1: An OpenAPI specification maintained alongside the application code.
bullets.b2: Operations identical to the ones of the web interface.
bullets.b3: Per-project authentication, suited to your automations.

sdk.title: The TypeScript SDK
sdk.lead: The SDK is generated from the API: it follows the same resources and the same version as the platform.

paragraphs.p1: The SDK is published as a package of the repository and updates with the API. It is used from a deployment script, a scheduled job or an internal integration.

bullets.b1: Generated from the OpenAPI specification, never written by hand.
bullets.b3: Published with the other packages of the repository.

cli.title: The Notploy CLI
cli.lead: The command line covers your deployments and your usual operations.

paragraphs.p1: The CLI talks to a Notploy server with the same credentials as the interface. It fits into a shell script, a continuous integration pipeline or an administration machine.

bullets.b1: Deploy and follow an application from a terminal.
bullets.b2: Drive the registered databases and servers.
bullets.b3: Work with the same permissions as the web interface.

mcp.title: The MCP server
mcp.lead: Notploy exposes a Model Context Protocol server, to drive the platform from an assistant.

paragraphs.p1: The MCP server gives a compatible assistant access to the operations of the platform, within the permissions you grant. It is published as a package of the repository.

bullets.b1: A package of the repository, installable next to the others.
bullets.b2: The same resources as the REST API.

integrations.title: In your tools, every day
integrations.lead: The platform integrates where you already work: your pipelines, your editor and your workstations.

githubActions.title: GitHub Actions
githubActions.desc: The integration package to trigger your deployments from GitHub.

vscode.title: VS Code extension
vscode.desc: An editor extension to follow and trigger your deployments.

clients.title: Desktop and mobile applications
clients.desc: The Electron and mobile clients to drive the platform outside the browser.

documentation.desc: The installation, configuration and operations guides.

templates.desc: Ready-to-deploy applications, curated by the project.

repository.desc: The full source code, the issues and the discussions.

meta.title: Notploy Cloud
meta.description: The Notploy platform operated for you, available on app.notploy.com, with no installation or maintenance on your side.

hero.title: The same platform, operated for you
hero.lead: Notploy Cloud serves the same application as your self-hosted installation, available on app.notploy.com.

what.title: One piece of software, two ways to operate it
what.lead: Notploy Cloud is not a separate edition: it is the application of the repository, run for you.

paragraphs.p1: Notploy is released under the MIT license. The code run by the cloud is the public repository's code: fixes, features and limits are therefore the same on both sides.
paragraphs.p2: You choose the cloud to avoid administering the platform itself — updates, the platform database, monitoring — while keeping control over your applications and the infrastructure that runs them.

bullets.b1: No closed edition: the same code as self-hosting.
bullets.b2: The platform is updated and monitored for you.
bullets.b3: Your applications stay deployed on the servers you register.
bullets.b4: You can move back to a self-hosted installation at any time.

differences.title: What the cloud takes care of
differences.lead: The three real differences between a self-hosted installation and the hosted offering.

runtime.title: The same engine
runtime.desc: The Notploy application, with the same deployments and the same databases.

tooling.title: No local deployment tooling
tooling.desc: The cloud image ships the application without the build tooling reserved for self-hosting.

updates.title: Updates taken care of
updates.desc: The platform is updated and watched without any action on your side.

start.title: Three steps to your first deployment
start.lead: The journey is the same as on a self-hosted installation, once the platform is in place.

account.title: Open your account
account.text: Create your account on app.notploy.com and complete the initial setup.

server.title: Register a machine
server.text: Add the server or the cluster that will run your applications, over SSH or Swarm.

deploy.title: Deploy
deploy.text: Connect a repository or a container image and start the first deployment.

start.notice: Keep your secrets out of the repository: environment variables are configured in the platform, never in the source code.

sovereignty.title: The cloud does not lock you in
sovereignty.lead: Because the project is open source, the hosted offering remains an option, not a dependency.

paragraphs.p1: Since the product and the hosted offering are the same software, moving to a self-hosted installation does not require rewriting your deployments. The documentation details the expected installation and configuration.

meta.title: Self-hosted
meta.description: Install Notploy yourself with Docker Compose: requirements, starting the stack, day-to-day operations and going to production.

hero.title: Install Notploy yourself
hero.lead: One Docker Compose stack, your hardware, your network: the self-hosted installation ships the complete deployment tooling.

requirements.title: What you need before you start
requirements.lead: The self-hosted installation runs in containers and drives the Docker engine of the host.

bullets.b1: Docker Engine with the Compose plugin, on the machine that will host Notploy.
bullets.b2: Access to the host Docker socket, required to build and manage workloads.
bullets.b3: That access is highly privileged: treat the machine as an administration server and do not expose it publicly before authentication and HTTPS are configured.

install.title: Four steps, one Compose file
install.lead: The repository provides the Compose file and a sample configuration to adapt.

clone.title: Get the repository
clone.text: Clone the project repository on the target machine, then move into the created directory.

configure.title: Configure the environment
configure.text: Copy the sample file to .env and set unique secrets, in particular the PostgreSQL password and the authentication key.

start.title: Start the stack
start.text: Build and start the containers with Docker Compose, then follow the logs of the application service.

setup.title: Complete the initial setup
setup.text: Open the platform on the indicated port and complete the initial setup.

install.notice: Keep the environment file private and never add it to the repository: it holds the secrets of your installation.

operations.title: The day-to-day commands
operations.lead: An installation is driven with the usual Compose commands.

paragraphs.p1: The platform data and its databases live in named volumes, preserved across restarts. The commands below cover the state of the services, their logs and stopping the stack.

bullets.b1: Check the state of the services of the stack.
bullets.b2: Follow the logs of the application or of a specific service.
bullets.b3: Stop the stack without deleting the data volumes.

production.title: Before opening the service
production.lead: An installation reachable from the Internet requires three things, in this order.

https.title: HTTPS
https.desc: Terminate encryption before any public exposure of the dashboard.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.desc: Create the administrator account and check the access rules before opening.

updates.title: Updates
updates.desc: Follow the release pace of the project to apply fixes.

meta.title: Security
meta.description: The security model of Notploy — privileged access to the Docker engine, authentication and TLS handled by the operator — and the private disclosure process.

hero.title: An explicit security model
hero.lead: Notploy drives workloads: its privileges, its limits and the disclosure process are documented here, with no grey areas.

model.title: The platform drives, you stay in control
model.lead: Notploy is not a multi-tenant service: it is a platform you run and you administer.

paragraphs.p1: A Notploy installation runs in containers and commands the Docker engine of the machine hosting it. That link is the condition of its operation: it is what allows images to be built and applications to be started.
paragraphs.p2: Authentication, networking and transport encryption are the operator's responsibility. The installation documentation describes the expected configuration before any public exposure.

privileges.title: Access to be treated as administrator access
privileges.lead: The privilege granted to the platform is real and must be limited accordingly.

bullets.b1: Access to the Docker socket is equivalent to root access on the host machine.
bullets.b2: Do not publish the dashboard before authentication and HTTPS are configured.
bullets.b3: Only grant that access to machines you actually administer.

reporting.title: Report a vulnerability privately
reporting.lead: Vulnerabilities are never reported in public issues.

paragraphs.p1: The SECURITY.md file of the repository describes the private disclosure process. Use it for any security flaw: it allows the problem to be fixed before disclosure.

bullets.b1: A private report, never a public issue.
bullets.b2: The useful technical details: reproduction, version, scope of the impact.

practices.title: Three reflexes for a healthy installation
practices.lead: Most of the risk is covered by configuration, not by patching.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.desc: Keep the environment file private and unique to each installation.

transport.title: Encryption
transport.desc: Terminate transport encryption before exposing the dashboard.

updates.title: Updates
updates.desc: Apply the project's releases, which fix known vulnerabilities.

meta.title: Accessibility
meta.description: Accessibility statement of the Notploy website: commitment, compliance status, non-accessible content, how the statement was established and remedies.

hero.title: Accessibility statement
hero.lead: The accessibility of the public website is a design commitment, not a last-minute addition: the website is built on a design system that carries accessibility requirements itself.
hero.notice: This statement covers the public website. The Notploy software and its documentation have their own feedback channels.

declaration.title: Our commitment
declaration.lead: The website aims to be usable without barriers by as many people as possible.

paragraphs.p1: This website relies on an accessible design system: semantic structure, verified contrast, keyboard navigation and explicit labels for assistive technologies. The components used carry those requirements by construction, which avoids reintroducing them page by page.
paragraphs.p2: Content is written in plain language and structured in titled sections, so that linear reading, like quick reading, both remain possible.

conformite.title: Compliance status
conformite.lead: The website is designed to meet the requirements that apply to information websites.

bullets.b1: Pages are structured with a single main heading and a continuous heading hierarchy.
bullets.b2: Keyboard navigation and skip links make it possible to reach the content and the footer.
bullets.b3: Colours and text sizes rely on design system tokens, designed for contrast.

nonAccessibles.title: Known non-accessible content
nonAccessibles.lead: Known limitations are declared here rather than left unsaid.

bullets.b1: Some figures and flow visualisations are graphic representations accompanied by an equivalent text, but remain difficult to grasp outside the visual.
bullets.b2: Video or animated content, where it exists, does not always come with a complete alternative.
bullets.b3: Downloadable documents may keep a layout produced by their authoring tool.

etablissement.title: How this statement was established
etablissement.lead: The conditions in which this statement was written.

tests.label: Tests performed
tests.value: Automated checks and a manual review of the main journeys

referentiel.label: Standard
referentiel.value: Web content accessibility guidelines (RGAA 4.1), target level AA

outils.label: Tools
outils.value: Browser accessibility analysis tools and manual checks

retour.title: Report an accessibility defect
retour.lead: A reported defect is a fixable defect.

paragraphs.p1: If part of the website is inaccessible to you, report it by describing the page, the action you attempted and the obstacle you met. Accessibility reports can go through the same channels as the other feedback on the website.

voiesRecours.title: Remedies
voiesRecours.lead: If the report stays unanswered, these routes remain open.

bullets.b1: Restore contact through another public channel of the project.
bullets.b2: Document the problem precisely (page, browser, assistive technology used).
bullets.b3: Refer the matter to the competent accessibility authority if no answer is received.
